newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-WINDIES RECALL WILLIAMS, NAME TWO NEWCOMERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WINDIES RECALL WILLIAMS, NAME TWO NEWCOMERS.

text.p: West Indies have recalled opener Stuart Williams and named two newcomers in a squad of 13 for the first test against India.
Leg-spinner Rawl Lewis and paceman Franklyn Rose are the uncapped pair included in the party for the opening match of the five-test series starting in Kingston, Jamaica, on March 6.
Openers Robert Samuels and Adrian Griffith, wicketkeeper Courtney Browne and pace bowler Patterson Thompson, who all went on the recent tour of Australia, have been overlooked.
Fast bowlers Kenneth Benjamin, Cameron Cuffy and Nixon McLean were ruled out by injury.
Williams, who played 12 tests between 1994 and 1995, scoring only 386 runs at an average of 22.70, gets back into the side after a successful West Indies A team tour of Sri Lanka last October.
Lewis, 22, bowled well on the A team tour of Sri Lanka, taking four for 23 to help West Indies win the second unofficial test against Sri Lanka.

The 25-year-old Rose returned to regional cricket for Jamaica this season after a self-imposed break and immediately made his mark with a man-of-the-match innings of 96 against the Leeward Islands in the opening match.
He so far has 18 Cup wickets after four matches, including five for 62 against Barbados last weekend.
India's 16-man squad, led Sachin Tendulkar, arrived in Jamaica late on Tuesday for the tour that also includes four one-day internationals.
The Indians open their itinerary on Friday with a four-day game against Jamaica at Sabina Park, Kingston.

West Indies squad: Stuart Williams, Sherwin Campbell, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Roland Holder, Junior Murray, Curtly Ambrose, Ian Bishop, Courtney Walsh (captain) Rawl Lewis, Franklyn Rose.
